prompts.title: Form: recent wins, draws and losses
prompts.prompt: Forma reciente — Brentford FC vs Liverpool FC. Vertical 9:16, charcoal #101412 ground. Legend top-left in warm white: Spanish heading 'FORMA RECIENTE' with 'Brentford FC' in lime #c5ed74 and 'Liverpool FC' in slate #8ca6bf. Lower quarter stays clear for permanent yellow subtitles; all action lives in the upper three quarters. Editorial variant (rhythmic kinetic typography): no axes. Centre-stage, the Spanish words 'VICTORIA', 'EMPATE', 'DERROTA' punch in on the narration beat, one at a time, alternating lime for Brentford and slate for Liverpool. Each word enters with a vertical snap from below, overshoots by a hair, settles with a subtle chromatic fringe; a thin lime/slate split line pulses beneath as a rhyme marker. Emphasis: the word 'EMPATE' gets a double-pulse because the voice stresses it; 'DERROTA' flashes then dims fast. Composition keeps one focal word at a time, centred slightly above the subtitle band. Camera: slow 9:16 push-in of a few fractions of scale with tiny parallax on the type. Transition: hard beat cut with a lime/slate diagonal wipe; exit: letters scatter into fine particles and drain toward the lower quarter margin. Statistical variant (grouped count bars): same charcoal ground. Spanish title 'VICTORIAS, EMPATES Y DERROTAS'. Two teams on a shared zero baseline, one bar per Spanish category 'Victorias', 'Empates', 'Derrotas', with values placed as {{home.wins}}, {{home.draws}}, {{home.losses}} and {{away.wins}}, {{away.draws}}, {{away.losses}}. Bars grow from the baseline with staggered entry left to right, lime for Brentford, slate for Liverpool; value counters tick up to the final numbers. A common scale in the same unit keeps the comparison honest; when sample sizes differ, a small Spanish 'muestra distinta' flag appears above the pair, otherwise a neutral tag shows 'muestra {{home.n}} · {{away.n}}' for both teams. A persistent source/sample strip sits just above the subtitle band: 'Fuente: Bzzoiro' with the sample reference rendered from the facts; both stay attached and are never converted into rates. Emphasis: the tallest column glows a fraction brighter and a thin lime outline traces its top edge. Camera: locked 9:16 with a gentle drift up as bars rise. Transition: cross-dissolve after the counters settle. Exit: bars retract to the baseline, leaving only the Spanish title before the cut.

prompts.title: Goals: for and against
prompts.prompt: Goles — Brentford FC vs Liverpool FC. Vertical 9:16, charcoal #101412. Spanish top heading 'GOLES', Brentford FC in lime #c5ed74, Liverpool FC in slate #8ca6bf. Lower quarter protected for permanent yellow subtitles. Editorial variant (illustrative pitch and ball path): a stylised half-pitch drawn in thin warm-white lines on charcoal, viewed from the side within 9:16. The pitch is generic; no invented match events. A lime ball leaves the Brentford third and traces a smooth arc; a slate ball answers from the Liverpool third along a mirrored path. The two arcs cross near the centre circle, one passing above the other, and each ball lands on a glowing Spanish word — 'A FAVOR' for the attacking path. When the narration contrasts the defensive end, a second layer of arcs curves back toward each goal, labelled 'RECIBIDOS', rendered in desaturated warm white so it reads as context, not celebration. Motion: arcs draw on with a trailing ribbon, ball spin hinted by a rotating seam; the crossing point flashes once. Emphasis: the lime ball holds the frame a fraction longer, giving the home side first focus. Camera: slow lateral dolly across the pitch, keeping the arcs on a comfortable 9:16 diagonal. Transition: speed-ramped wipe along the arc; exit: arcs flatten into a single horizontal line that fades into the lower quarter margin. Statistical variant (paired bars, shared scale): Spanish title 'GOLES A FAVOR Y RECIBIDOS'. Two colour-coded rows: Brentford in lime and Liverpool in slate. Each row has a pair of horizontal bars sharing one scale in the same unit: 'A favor' and 'Recibidos'. Values appear as {{home.gf}} and {{home.ga}} for Brentford, {{away.gf}} and {{away.ga}} for Liverpool. Bars grow from a common left zero baseline; counters tick up in warm white. A centre hairline grid marks equal steps so the paired comparison is read at a glance. Sample sizes remain attached: a small Spanish note above the bars shows 'muestra {{home.n}} · {{away.n}}', with unit and source rendered from the catalog. A persistent source strip reads 'Fuente: Bzzoiro' just above the subtitle band. Emphasis: when the away 'Recibidos' bar reaches its end, it gets a one-frame slate pulse, then settles. Camera: locked 9:16 with a small tilt down as the last bar completes. Transition: wipe from the bars into the next scene. Exit: bars retract to baseline, title holds, then fades.

prompts.title: Clean sheets: count comparison
prompts.prompt: Arcos en cero — Brentford FC vs Liverpool FC. Vertical 9:16, charcoal #101412, warm white #edf0e6 typography, lime #c5ed74 for Brentford FC and slate #8ca6bf for Liverpool FC. Spanish heading 'ARCOS EN CERO'. Lower quarter reserved for permanent yellow subtitles. Editorial variant (defensive energy and stylised shield): a single abstract shield, split lime and slate, forms at centre frame in the upper three quarters. It is built from two overlapping plates; the lime plate clicks in first, the slate plate slots behind it. A pulse wave of warm-white rings expands from the crest each time the narration stresses a defensive stop. No scoreboards, no invented saves. Spanish micro-labels 'SÓLIDO' and 'FIRME' breathe in and out near the shield edge, never claiming a match event. Motion: the shield rotates a few degrees around its vertical axis, subtle chromatic edge light, rings travelling outward and dissolving before the lower quarter. Emphasis: the crest line brightens once, holding one clear focal point. Camera: slow 9:16 orbit, roughly a quarter turn, keeping the shield centred. Transition: the shield splits down the middle and slides apart to reveal the next scene. Exit: both halves drift outward and fade. Statistical variant (count comparison, not rates): Spanish title 'ARCOS EN CERO · RECUENTO'. Two vertical columns with a shared zero baseline: Brentford in lime, Liverpool in slate. Bar heights are counts of clean sheets, labelled with {{home.clean}} and {{away.clean}}; counters tick up in warm white. A single horizontal reference line marks the top of the lower count so the eye reads the gap without any rate conversion. Beside each column a Spanish caption shows the sample: 'muestra {{home.n}}' and 'muestra {{away.n}}', with unit and source rendered from catalog metadata; nothing is divided or annualised. A persistent source/sample strip above the subtitle band reads 'Fuente: Bzzoiro'. Emphasis: the leading column's outline gets a thin warm-white trace and a soft lime or slate glow, while the other stays flat. Camera: locked 9:16 with a small drift upward as the counters settle. Transition: cross-dissolve on the beat. Exit: columns retract to baseline, leaving the Spanish title before the cut.

prompts.title: Head-to-head history
prompts.prompt: Cruces previos — Brentford FC vs Liverpool FC. Vertical 9:16, charcoal #101412, warm white #edf0e6, lime #c5ed74 for Brentford FC, slate #8ca6bf for Liverpool FC. Spanish heading 'CRUCES PREVIOS'. Lower quarter kept clear for permanent yellow subtitles. Historical data is not a forecast; no predictive claim is made. Editorial variant (visual duel): both clubs appear as opposing silhouettes — a lime crest-like emblem on the left, a slate one on the right — facing each other across a narrow warm-white seam down the centre of the 9:16 frame. On the narration beat, the two emblems lean in, clash once at the seam, and recoil; a ring of warm-white sparks flares at the contact point. The clash repeats with lower amplitude, as a memory of the series rather than a live event. Spanish tags 'DUELO' and 'HISTORIA' breathe into the margins, never labelling a specific result. Motion: parallax between the two emblems, the seam flickering like a taut wire as each side pushes. Emphasis: the slate emblem holds a fraction longer on the second clash, matching the emphasis in the voice. Camera: slow 9:16 dolly along the seam, no axis labels. Transition: the seam snaps shut and the frame cuts to the statistical card. Exit: emblems dissolve into fine graphite particles. Statistical variant (historical win/draw comparison): Spanish title 'VICTORIAS Y EMPATES EN CRUCES'. A horizontal row per team shares one zero baseline and the same unit: Brentford's row shows 'Victorias' as {{h2h.homeWins}} in lime, Liverpool's row shows 'Victorias' as {{h2h.awayWins}} in slate, and a neutral warm-white segment 'Empates' carries {{h2h.draws}}. The sample is stated explicitly above the chart as 'muestra {{h2h.total}}' rendered from the catalog, with source metadata shown in a persistent 'Fuente: Bzzoiro' strip just above the subtitle band. Bars grow from left zero with staggered counters; a thin centre hairline helps compare segment lengths without converting anything to a rate. Emphasis: the longer 'Victorias' segment pulses once in its team colour while the other stays calm; the 'Empates' segment remains neutral. Camera: locked 9:16 with a gentle upward drift as the counters land. Transition: wipe on the beat into the next scene. Exit: segments retract to the baseline, leaving only the Spanish heading.

prompts.title: Synthesis: equal attack, different defence
prompts.prompt: Síntesis — Brentford FC vs Liverpool FC. Vertical 9:16, charcoal #101412, warm white #edf0e6, lime #c5ed74 for Brentford FC, slate #8ca6bf for Liverpool FC. Spanish heading 'LA TENSIÓN'. Lower quarter reserved for permanent yellow subtitles. No model estimate is drawn: none is published in the catalog. Editorial variant (team reveals, narrative emphasis): the frame opens on a dark charcoal field. A lime vertical column of light rises from the lower-left, revealing the Spanish name 'BRENTFORD FC'; a slate column answers from the lower-right with 'LIVERPOOL FC'. Both meet at centre and become two translucent panes that overlap — the overlap area glows warm white, carrying the Spanish phrase 'MISMO ATAQUE, DISTINTA DEFENSA'. The narration's key words are echoed as small Spanish type in the margins: 'ATAQUE' and 'DEFENSA'. Motion: reveals are driven by rising light columns, each with a fine grain texture; the overlap glow breathes once and holds. Emphasis: a single warm-white pulse crosses the overlap on the stressed syllable. Camera: slow 9:16 push-in, keeping the two names in the upper three quarters. Transition: the panes rotate slightly and dissolve into the statistical frame. Exit: light columns fade down before the cut. Statistical variant (paired goal bars, shared scale): Spanish title 'GOLES A FAVOR Y EN CONTRA'. Two colour-coded rows, Brentford in lime and Liverpool in slate, each with paired horizontal bars sharing one scale in the same unit: 'A favor' and 'En contra'. Values render as {{home.gf}} and {{home.ga}}, then {{away.gf}} and {{away.ga}}; counters tick up from a common left zero baseline in warm white. The tension is read directly: attacking bars land almost level while defensive bars separate clearly. A thin centre hairline and equal step marks keep the comparison legible. Sample and source stay attached: a Spanish strip above the subtitle band reads 'muestra {{home.n}} · {{away.n}}' with 'Fuente: Bzzoiro' rendered from catalog metadata; a Spanish label 'histórico reciente' marks the window, and no unit is mixed and nothing is converted to a rate. Emphasis: the away 'En contra' bar glows slate on completion, while the home 'En contra' bar stays flat. Camera: locked 9:16, tiny upward drift. Transition: cross-dissolve on the beat. Exit: bars retract left to zero, title holds, then fades.
